title: Apple-style motion
summary: Springs instead of fixed curves, interruptible, immediate feedback.

overview.purpose: Make web motion feel fluid like Apple’s: spring-driven, interruptible and responsive.
overview.when: Adding transitions, gestures, press feedback or scroll-linked motion.
takeaways: Fade instead of move for reduced motion

sections.title: Springs
sections.intro: A spring is described by how quickly it responds and how much it bounces.

items.title: Smooth
items.more: Apple’s default for UI chrome: sheets, overlays, navigation.

items.title: Snappy
items.more: Toggles, chips, small state changes around 200–300 ms.

items.title: Bouncy
items.more: Playful moments and drag release only. Not for chrome.

items.title: CSS linear() springs
items.text: Sample the spring into a curve.
items.more: Generate the points from spring parameters (for example with kvin.me/css-springs) and use them as an easing.

items.title: Durations
items.more: Toggle 200–300 ms, full-screen push 350–450 ms, large reveal 400–500 ms. Micro-interactions under 250 ms feel instant.

sections.title: Fluid interfaces
sections.intro: Three traits from Apple’s fluid-interface talks.

items.title: Responsive
items.more: React on pointerdown, not after a timeout. Never block input behind an animation.

items.title: Interruptible
items.more: A new target starts from where the element is now. CSS transitions do this; keyframes do not.

items.title: Velocity handoff
items.more: The release speed of a drag becomes the spring’s initial velocity, so motion continues naturally.

items.title: Feedback on every action
items.more: Scale or dim on press. Web vibration does not work in iOS Safari, so never rely on it.

sections.title: Reduced motion
sections.intro: Keep the meaning, drop the movement.

items.title: Fade, don’t fly
items.text: Swap the move for an opacity change.
items.more: With reduced motion, a sheet fades in place instead of sliding.

items.title: Gate pointer sugar
items.text: Magnetic and tilt only on fine pointers.
